Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:41: Likewise, at his meals, his celebrations, his festivals, his appointed times, and in his sukkah, she should not enter and should not mingle with him, and he should invite the poor, who are a dwelling place for holiness, as is known. And his charity should precede all his affairs, since with that single coin, holiness is immediately present. He should not utter with his mouth anything against Satan, nor mention him, nor speak in anger, which is an offering to him, and the like. He should not curse himself, nor say "let it become for Satan" or "in an evil hour" and the like, since speech causes great harm. He should not frighten a small child by saying, "a cat will take you," "a camel will take you," "a dog will take you, it will bite you," and the like, for this is called by the name of dog and cat and all the evil names to cause harm. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:42: It remains for us to explain the proper times for the holiness of union, to draw down holy souls. The proper time is at midnight or after midnight, for ordinary people; and for Torah scholars, on Friday night at midnight or after midnight — and we have already copied the words of the Zohar above in chapter 7.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:43: Regarding what my teacher, peace be upon him, wrote — that the first preparation for union is a person's purification from his sins — Rashbi, peace be upon him, likewise explained (Zohar, portion Bereshit, 54a), which we copied above in chapter 5, that just as a person is drawn, so he draws a soul to his heart: if he is drawn after holiness he draws a holy soul, and if, God forbid, he is drawn after impurity, he likewise draws an impure soul from the Other Side.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:44: Therefore, besides the repentance one must do at the time of conception, one must precede it with repentance so that a fit woman become available to him and his seed emerge pure without waste — as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, portion Vayechi, 229a), on the verse, "the angel who redeems me from all evil" (Genesis 48:16). These are his words: Rabbi Chiya opened and said (Proverbs 19:14), "house and wealth are an inheritance from fathers" — is it truly an inheritance from fathers? Does not the Holy One, blessed be He, give everything to a person, and once a person has inherited a house and money, he sometimes bequeaths it all to his son and it becomes an inheritance from fathers? But "a prudent wife is from the LORD" — because when a person inherits a wife, he inherits her from the Holy One, blessed be He, for the Holy One, blessed be He, does not assign a woman to a person except when it is proclaimed of her in the firmament, for the Holy One, blessed be He, pairs matches before they come into the world; and when people are found worthy according to their deeds, a wife is given to them accordingly, and everything is revealed before the Holy One, blessed be He, and according to the deeds of the worthy, matches are so paired. Sometimes matches ascend into the balance-scales, and that person deviates from his way; his match rises for another until his deeds become fit; and when his deeds become fit, or his time arrives, one man is pushed aside before another man, and this one comes and takes what was his — and this is difficult before the Holy One, blessed be He, more than anything, to push a person aside before another man. Therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, gives a wife to a person, and matches come from Him; therefore, "a prudent wife is from the LORD" — for the Holy One, blessed be He, gives everything to a person.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:45: And should you say, "a prudent wife" and not another — come and see: even though the Holy One, blessed be He, prepares good things for a person to give him, if he deviates from his way, from being with the Holy One, blessed be He, toward the other side, from that other side to which he attached himself will come to him whatever comes, all accusations and all evils, and they do not come to him from the Holy One, blessed be He, but from that evil side to which he attached himself through the deeds he did. Therefore, regarding a wife who is not prudent, King Solomon, peace be upon him, said of this (Ecclesiastes 7:26), "and I find more bitter than death, the woman" etc. — because it is through a person's sins that he draws this upon himself, through the deeds he did. And when the Holy One, blessed be He, is pleased with a person because of his fit deeds, He arranges for him a wife who is prudent and redeems him with redemption from the other side; therefore Jacob said (Genesis 48:16), "the angel who redeems me from all evil" — that a wife from the other side was not arranged for me, and no unfitness occurred in my seed, for all [my children] are righteous and complete in every completeness, because he was redeemed from all evil, and Jacob did not attach himself to that other side at all; therefore, "the angel who redeems me from all evil." Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:46: Behold, a person does not merit his true mate from the side of holiness until his deeds improve — as in the matter of Jacob, who, because he did not attach himself to the evil side, merited his true mate and his seed emerged pure without waste. For the woman is like the land: if a person does not sow in fit land, it will not produce good growth; but if the land is fit for sowing, it will produce growth properly. Therefore repentance and prayer are needed, as it is said (Psalms 32:6), "for this let every pious one pray to You at a time when he may be found" — and they said (Berachot 8a), "at a time when he may be found" refers to a wife. Thus we see that besides being pious, prayer is also needed. The reason is that when a person has not yet encountered his true mate, he must return through reincarnation until he encounters her, and all his labor is found to be in vain — as is explained in the Zohar, portion Mishpatim.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:47: And in Tikkunim (30a) it says: this sin, that a person mixes the firstborn drop with confusion [foreign matter], causes another to take his true mate, and this is measure for measure; therefore (Exodus 23:19), "the first of the firstfruits of your land you shall bring to the house of the LORD your God; you shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk" — for that son who is a mixture, who issues as a mixed kind [kilayim] from a woman not truly his, is against him [measure for measure]. Therefore, one who merits [proper union], an "ezer" [helper] is made for him — his true mate, who is a helper to him in Torah, in the commandment, in awe, in love — a helper to him in this world and in the World to Come. But if not, another who is not truly his is against him, to destroy him from both worlds — and all this is caused because he did not guard his first drop for his true mate. Nevertheless, if he returns in repentance, it is said (Isaiah 6:10), "and he shall return and be healed," and he is given his true mate, of whom it is said (Proverbs 3:8), "it shall be healing to your navel" — and she is the image of Torah, which is medicine and life, as it is written (ibid. 3:18), "she is a tree of life to those who grasp her," and the woman is her image, as it is written (Ecclesiastes 9:9), "enjoy life with the wife whom you love." Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:48: Further, in Tikkun 15 (30b), these are his words: and the secret of the matter — whoever disgraces bread, the crumbs of bread which are drops the size of an olive, poverty pursues him; rather he must guard his own drops so as not to cast them in a place where they are not needed. And therefore the masters of the Mishnah established: honor your wives so that you may become wealthy — meaning, honor them by guarding the first drop so as not to make it waste. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:49: It remains for us to explain the times specifically proper for the holiness of union, to draw down holy souls. The proper time is at midnight for the rest of the people, or after midnight; and for Torah scholars, on Friday night at midnight or after midnight — and we have already copied the words of the Zohar above in chapter 7.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:50: Further, they said in Midrash HaNe'elam, portion Vayera (112a), these are his words: Rabbi Yosef, when he went down to Babylon, saw those young unmarried men who would go among beautiful women and not sin. He said to them, do you not fear the evil inclination? They said, we do not come from an impure origin — we are circumcised from the holiest of the holy, for Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav: a person must sanctify himself at the time of relations, and holy, worthy children issue from him who do not fear the evil inclination, as it is said (Leviticus 20:7), "and you shall sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy." Rabbi Abba said: what is the meaning of what is written (Ezekiel 20:20), "and sanctify My Sabbaths"? Rather, the conjugal duty of Torah scholars is only from Sabbath to Sabbath, and it warns them, since marital relations for the sake of a mitzvah is meant, "sanctify" — meaning, sanctify yourselves on My Sabbaths in that marital relation of mitzvah. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:51: And they were strict in the Zohar (portion Tazria, 49b) regarding one who does not practice this holiness, saying that one who unites with his wife before midnight draws a soul from the Other Side, and of him it is said (Proverbs 19:2), "also, without knowledge, the soul is not good," and likewise "and he who hastens with his feet sins." He said, one who hastens and rushes the moment without holy intent certainly sins in everything. And he said that of this it is said (Psalms 32:9), "be not like a horse or a mule without understanding" — and he said, in what do people differ from a horse and a mule? In their own holiness, to be found whole and marked out entirely; and he said that of this the Torah commanded, "and you shall sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy" — if they distance themselves [from this practice], where is their holiness? For this reason one must rebuke his inclination, and if [lustful] thoughts come, he should nullify them with words of Torah, which is the antidote for the evil inclination, and remember for himself the day of death. Nevertheless, one must be cunning with fear: if he sees that his inclination is overpowering him and he is about to emit seed in vain, it is better to transgress a positive commandment [by hastening] rather than a prohibition, which is called "evil" and liable to death and the other punishments to be explained in their place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:52: Further, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (portion Bereshit, 49b) the proper times for union. These are his words: Rabbi Shimon opened and said, "and he went on his journeys [lemas'av] from the Negev to Beit-El, to the place where his tent had been at first, between Beit-El and Ai" (Genesis 13:3). "And he went on his journeys" — it should have said "on his journey" [singular]; what is "his journeys" [plural]? Rather, there are two journeys, one his and one the Shechinah's — for every person must be found male and female together, in order to strengthen faith, and then the Shechinah never separates from him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:53: And should you say, one who goes out on the road where male and female are not found together, the Shechinah separates from him — come and see: one who goes out on the road and arranges his prayer before the Holy One, blessed be He, in order to draw the Shechinah of his Master upon him before he departs, at a time when male and female are found together — once he has arranged his prayer and his praise and the Shechinah rests upon him, let him depart, for the Shechinah unites with him so that male and female be found — male and female in the town, male and female in the field. This is what is written (Psalms 85:14), "righteousness shall go before him and shall set his footsteps on the way."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:54: Come and see: all the while a person delays on the road he must guard his deeds, so that the supernal union not separate from him and a blemish be found without male and female — in the town it is needed when his wife is with him, and all the more so here, where the supernal union is bound to him; moreover, this union guards him on his road and does not separate from him until he returns to his house. At the time he enters his house, he must gladden his house, since his house caused him that supernal union; once he comes to her, he must gladden her for two reasons: one, because of the joy of that union, which is the joy of a mitzvah, the joy of the Shechinah; and moreover, that it increases peace below — this is what is written (Job 5:24), "and you shall know that your tent is at peace, and you shall visit your habitation and not sin" — does he sin if he does not visit his wife? Indeed so, for he thereby diminishes the honor of the supernal union that united with him — his wife caused it for him. And the other reason: if his wife conceives, the supernal union pours a holy soul into it, for this covenant is called the covenant of the Holy One, blessed be He. Therefore he must intend this joy just as he must intend the joy of Shabbat — those who are wise [know this]; therefore, "and you shall know that your tent is at peace," for the Shechinah comes with you and rests in your house; therefore, "and you shall visit your habitation and not sin" — what is "and not sin"? To perform before the Holy One, blessed be He, the joy of the mitzvah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:55: In like manner, Torah scholars who separate from their wives all the days of the week in order to occupy themselves with Torah — the supernal union unites with them and does not separate from them, since male and female are found [united in this higher sense]; once Shabbat enters, Torah scholars must gladden their households for the honor of the supernal union, and direct their hearts with the will of their Master, as has been said.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:56: In like manner, one whose wife is in her days of impurity, and he guards her properly — all those days the supernal union unites with him and male and female are found [united above]; when his wife becomes purified, he must gladden her with the joy of the mitzvah, the supernal joy. And all these reasons we have mentioned ascend to a single level; in short, all these people of faith must direct their heart and will toward this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:57: Further, regarding the matter of a person's union with his wife, what Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman [Ramban], of blessed memory, composed (Iggeret HaKodesh): know that since the nation of Israel is dedicated to the Holy One, blessed be He, and He has separated it, through His holy Torah, from all the nations who worship idols — just as He, blessed be He, is separate from all that is besides Him, as He, blessed be He, said (Isaiah 43:21), "this people I formed for Myself" etc., and He said elsewhere, "the LORD is one," by verbal analogy [gezerah shavah] — and this is what we say [in the Shabbat afternoon prayer], "You are one and Your Name is one, and who is like Your people Israel, one nation." And afterward it says, "I formed for Myself" — meaning, I separated for Myself, to be dedicated to My honor, as He said (Leviticus 20:26), "and I have separated you from the peoples to be Mine."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:58: And you already know that servants conduct themselves according to what they see in the conduct of their master; and He, blessed be He, who is our Master and we His servants — behold, He is holy, and there is none holy like Him, and He commanded us to be holy as He is holy, and our Sages of blessed memory explained regarding the verse (Deuteronomy 28:9), "and you shall walk in His ways": just as He is merciful, so you be merciful; just as He is gracious, so you be gracious. If so, we find that all of Israel's conduct is founded upon the unification of the great Name, blessed be He; therefore they resemble Him in all their deeds, and He, blessed be He, said (Leviticus 20:7), "and you shall sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy." Since all our deeds are in the likeness of the deeds of the Name, blessed be He, we find that whenever we do what is good and right, we sanctify His great Name, as He said (Deuteronomy 4:8), "and what great nation is there that has statutes" etc. — since we resemble our Creator, blessed be He; and whenever we do not conduct ourselves properly and all our deeds are corrupt, we profane the Name of Heaven through them, since we resemble Him, and our deeds are ugly. Regarding this they said in tractate Yoma (86a): when a person reads Scripture, studies Mishnah, and conducts his business dealings honestly, of him the verse says (Isaiah 49:3), "and He said to me, You are My servant" etc.; but when a person reads Scripture and studies Mishnah and his business dealings are not honest, what do people say of him? "See so-and-so, how corrupt are his ways and deeds" — and of him the verse says (Jeremiah 36:20), "these are the people of the LORD, and yet they have gone out of His land," and the Name of Heaven is found to be profaned. The reason for all this, as we have said, is that since we resemble Him in our deeds, the holiness of the Name and its profanation depend on our deeds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:59: Now that we have informed you of all this, know that since the matter and nature of a person is the cause of his being evil or good, according to the constitution of the mixture from which the drop that formed him arose, and his union is found to be the cause of the sanctification of the Name or its profanation, according to the children he begets — He commanded us regarding this and warned us, saying that we must sanctify ourselves at the time of relations, as the tradition comes on the verse (Leviticus 15:31), "and you shall separate the children of Israel [from their impurity]." And because this is a cause for a person to beget righteous children who sanctify the Name of Heaven [we must be careful in this].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:60: Since this is so, you need to know what we have said, that a person must sanctify himself at the time of relations, and this holiness divides into five parts: the first way, in the nature of the union; the second way, in the timing of the union; the third way, in the food fitting for union; the fourth way, in the intent of the union; the fifth way, in the manner of the union. I shall now proceed to explain these matters sufficiently for the intent proper to each.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:61: The first way, in the nature of the union
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:62: Know that this union is a holy and clean matter when it is done as it should be, at the proper time, and with the proper intent, and a person should not think that in proper union there is disgrace or ugliness, God forbid — for proper union is called "knowledge" [de'ah], and it is not for nothing that it is so called (1 Samuel 1:19), "and Elkanah knew Chanah his wife" etc. — this is the secret of the drop of seed, when it is drawn from the place of knowledge and understanding, which is the brain. And know that if there were not great holiness in this matter, union would not be called "knowledge." The Name, blessed be He, created everything as His wisdom decreed, and did not create anything that would be disgraceful or ugly — for if one were to say that union is a disgraceful matter, behold, the organs of intercourse are organs of disgrace, yet the Name, blessed be He, created them by His word, as it is written (Deuteronomy 32:6), "He made you and established you," and our Sages of blessed memory said in tractate Chullin (56b) that the Holy One, blessed be He, created "stabilizers" [konniyot] in man. And in Midrash Kohelet (2:15) they said, "[that which] he has already made" (Ecclesiastes 2:12) teaches that He and His court took a census of every single limb and set it in its proper place; and if the organs of intercourse were organs of disgrace, how could the Name, blessed be He, create something that has any deficiency or disgrace, God forbid? Rather, the deeds of the Holy One, blessed be He, are perfect, as it is said (Deuteronomy 32:4), "the Rock, His work is perfect," and the Name, blessed be He, has "eyes too pure to look upon evil" (Habakkuk 1:13); there is no matter of flaw or disgrace before Him — He created man and woman, and created every single organ within them and prepared them according to their design, and did not create in them anything disgraceful.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:63: The clear testimony to this is what is said in the account of creation (Genesis 2:25), "and the two of them were naked" etc. — all this was before they sinned, since they were occupied with intellectual matters and all their intent was toward Heaven, and these organs were no different in their eyes than the eyes or other limbs of the body; but when they turned after bodily pleasures and did not intend for the sake of Heaven, it says (ibid. 3:7), "and they knew that they were naked." And the explanation is: just as hands, when they write a Torah scroll in purity, are honored and praiseworthy, but when they steal or do something disgraceful they are disgraceful, so were the organs of intercourse of the man and his wife before they sinned; and just as every single organ has praise and honor in doing good and disgrace in doing evil, so it was for Adam with the organs of intercourse.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:64: We find, then, that all the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, are justice, purity, and cleanliness, and that all ugliness comes entirely from the side of man's action. Regarding this Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Ecclesiastes 7:29), "only see this have I found, that God made man" etc. — meaning, there is nothing in any of man's organs, from the side of creation, that is a flaw or disgrace, for everything, in supernal wisdom, is a fitting, good, and beautiful thing; but man, in his foolishness, brings disgrace into things that had no disgrace from the beginning. Understand this well.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:65: Now, the secret of "knowledge" [de'ah] to which I allude is the secret that man is composed of the secret of Chochmah, Binah, and Da'at — for man is the secret of Da'at, and this is the secret of man and woman according to the ways of the inner tradition. If so, the matter of union is a matter of great elevation when done properly, and our Sages of blessed memory said: at the time a person unites with his wife in holiness, the Shechinah rests between them — the secret of man and woman, when they become warmed, if the Shechinah departs from between them, there remains fire and fire, as we learn in Sotah (17a): Rabbi Akiva used to expound, man and woman — if they merit, the Shechinah is between them; if they do not merit, fire consumes them. Meaning: when a person unites with his wife in holiness, the Shechinah is between them — you find in the name of "ish" [man] the letter yod, and in the name of "ishah" [woman] the letter heh — behold, this is the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, present between them. But if they did not intend union for holiness but only to fill their desire, and became warmed through desire and craving, then the yod of the man's name and the heh of the woman's name, which is Yah, is removed from between them, and there remains fire and fire. And our Sages of blessed memory intended this secret when they said (Niddah 31a): there are three partners in a person, and they are: man, woman, and the Holy One, blessed be He. And if the matter were disgraceful, how could they have included the Name, blessed be He, in something that is so?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:66: Now, the Name, blessed be He, said to Abraham regarding the birth of Isaac, "and I will bless her, and I will also give you a son from her" (Genesis 17:17), and regarding Rebecca, "and Isaac entreated the LORD" etc. (ibid. 25:22), and regarding Rachel and Leah, "and He opened her womb" (ibid. 29:31; 30:22), and regarding Elkanah, etc.; and among the general blessings, "there shall be no woman who miscarries or is barren" (Exodus 23:26). And further we learn in Chagigah, three keys were not given into the hand of an agent, and one of them is [that of] conception, as it is said, "and He opened her womb" etc. And if the matter were disgraceful, why would the Holy One, blessed be He, do it without an agent?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:67: And in Bereshit Rabbah (85:8): "and he turned to her by the way" (Genesis 38:16) — Judah wished to pass by, [but] the Holy One, blessed be He, signaled to the angel appointed over desire. This comes to inform us that the intent and desire of the Name, blessed be He, was in this union, and therefore twins were born, both righteous, both pure, like the pattern of sun and moon, Peretz and Zerach; understand that they were born in the pattern of the orders of the world, and there is no disgrace in their union, just as there is no disgrace in the establishment of the orders of the world, in general and in particular.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:68: And regarding Ruth it is said (Ruth 4:13), "and the LORD gave her conception" etc. — and if there were disgrace in the matter, it is already said (Habakkuk 1:13), "Your eyes are too pure to look upon evil." Rather, when the union is for the sake of Heaven, there is nothing more holy and clean than it above, and therefore it is said regarding the union of the righteous (Jeremiah 1:5), "before I formed you in the womb, I knew you" etc. But with the wicked and lawless, that entire drop is impure, and the Name has no portion in it, and of it is said (Psalms 58:4), "the wicked are estranged from the womb." But regarding the union of a man with his wife properly, our Sages of blessed memory explained that it is like the pattern of heaven and earth, as it is said (Zechariah 12:1), "the utterance of the LORD, who stretches out the heavens and lays the foundation of the earth, and forms the spirit of man within him," and it says (Amos 9:6), "and has founded His band upon the earth" — they are a single band to create man. This is [the meaning of] "let us make man in our image" (Genesis 1:26) — meaning, I too am a partner in the creation of man; and this partnership is that all the orders of the body are drawn from the father and mother, and the Name, blessed be He, casts into him a soul, as He said (ibid. 2:7), "and He blew into his nostrils the breath of life," and it says (Ecclesiastes 12:7), "and the dust returns to the earth as it was" etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:69: Now that we have informed you of the secret of the first way of union, we shall inform you of the second way, which is the opposite of the first: for when a person does not intend for the sake of Heaven, that drawn seed is a putrid drop in which the Name has no portion, and it is called one who "destroys his way upon the earth," and his whole body is [dedicated] to terror; it is as though he plants an asherah and fattens calves for idolatry, since it is a corrupted seed, a drop cast into a foul channel — of him it is said (Psalms 58:4), "the wicked are estranged from the womb." And the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded in the Torah, saying (Leviticus 20:26), "and you shall be holy to Me" etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:70: The second gate, on the timing of the union
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:71: Now, the Name, blessed be He, said in the Torah (Exodus 21:10), "her food, her clothing, and her conjugal rights he shall not diminish," and the conjugal duty [onah] spoken of in the Torah is explained in the Gemara (Ketubot 61b), for the frequency of conjugal duty varies according to the situation of each person. For now let us set aside the discussion of the conjugal duty of ordinary people and speak of the proper conjugal duty of Torah scholars, which is from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve; and of this it is said (Psalms 1:3), "who gives his fruit in its season" etc. — this is the conjugal duty of Torah scholars (cf. Ketubot 62b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:72: Know that a person's seed is the life of his body and the light of its radiance, for it is the choicest and purest blood in the body — were it not so, the form of man would not exist through it. Behold, the seed is a component of the body and has a share from every single organ, for it is known that an ear will not be born from an eye nor an eye from an ear, but each organ is drawn from the nature of a similar organ, just as beans and lentils will not sprout from wheat seed, nor a donkey, ox, or sheep from human seed — every organ and every form has its own particular nature and known power from which it is born, and one need not worry about a blind man begetting a sighted one, since the power of the organ is present in the general nature that is in the body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:73: If so, the seed is a component of every single organ of the body, and it is not fitting for a person to be with his wife as frequently as a rooster, for then his strength would weaken and the light of his eyes diminish, and all the components of his organs would waste away. But when the union takes place at the known conjugal time, from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve, which is the secret of the turning of the celestial spheres forward and backward over the seven days of the week, then he can bestow strength upon another without himself lacking anything that would leave him visibly weakened, since he has already received strength from which he can bestow. Therefore it says (Psalms 1:3), "who gives his fruit in its season" — that is, from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve — and adjacent to it, "and his leaf shall not wither," meaning that the union should be for the sake of Heaven and come to a completed act.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:74: The reason it is from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve is that Shabbat is the foundation of the world and the pattern of the world of souls, because of the reason "Shabbat for the LORD"; and Torah scholars intended, from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve, to beget a form fit for the service of the Creator, blessed be He, possessing a pure, supernal, intellectual soul, as He said (Exodus 31:17), "and on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed [vayinafash]." This, then, is the intent in the conjugal timing of Torah scholars; understand this well, for they did not set their conjugal time on the physical days, namely the six days of labor, but on the day that is entirely Shabbat and the world of souls.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:75: Now that we have aroused you to this, let us return to what we intended to arrange: the timing of union divides into three parts. The first part, conjugal timing regarding the days; the second, the timing of conjugal duty with respect to food; the third, the timing of conjugal duty with respect to the hours. The first part we have already explained in this chapter; the second of the three parts, the timing of conjugal duty with respect to food, you will need to know, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:76: Know that the food a person is nourished by requires three kinds of transformation, and at the fourth stage it becomes seed, or white blood that nourishes the body. If a person has relations soon after eating, at that time the body's nature is boiling, and the blood is mixed and not pure and clear; and that drop drawn from him is then turbid, soiled, putrid, and filthy — not clean nor pure — and the child from that drop is found to be from a turbid and filthy foundation, and of it is said (Job 15:35), "they conceive mischief and bear iniquity," and it says (Psalms 58:4), "the wicked are estranged from the womb" — since the nature of the mixture of a drop that is not pure necessarily makes what is formed from it detestable and filthy.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:77: Therefore a person must time union for an hour when his soul is settled upon him, and the body's nature has quieted from the boiling of the food he ate, and the blood has been refined and the fluids have descended to their natural place, and then the elements of the body are arranged in proper order — this being reserved for the last half of the night. Regarding this our Sages of blessed memory said in tractate Berachot (5b): Abba Binyamin says, all my days I was troubled about two things: about my bed, that it be placed between north and south, etc.; and Rabbi Yitzchak said, whoever places his bed between north and south will have male children, as it is said (Psalms 17:14), "and Your treasure [tzefunecha, from tzafon, north] fills their belly; they are satisfied with sons" etc. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: also his wife will not miscarry, as it is written here, "fills their belly," and it is written there (Genesis 25:24), "and her days were fulfilled to give birth" etc. And I must arouse you regarding this matter: it is known that no fool or simpleton in the world thinks that merely because a bed is placed between north and south a person merits male children and that his wife will not miscarry — all the more so, how could the pillars of the world, wise and understanding men, say such things? Rather, they spoke words alluded to, as is their good custom everywhere, and I shall explain: it is known that intense cold is toward the northern direction, and intense heat toward the southern direction, and the sages of truth know that a person's inclination toward extremes is not the way of good and right, but the intermediate qualities are the choicest — as Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Ecclesiastes 7:16-17), "be not overly righteous, and be not overly wicked, and be not a fool." And since north and south are two opposites of heat and cold, they concealed their words and alluded to them, saying that one who has relations while the constitution of his body is balanced between heat and cold — then his natural functions can be at rest and he will not ejaculate quickly, but can engage and wait, and then the woman achieves emission [of her own seed] first, and the woman's seed is found to be like the pattern of matter, and when the man's seed then comes, it is found like the pattern of the craftsman who fashions a form in matter. This is the secret of what our Sages of blessed memory said (cf. Niddah 71a): as a reward for the righteous delaying [their emission] over the woman's womb, they have male children, as it is said (Psalms 127:3), "behold, children are an inheritance of the LORD" etc. And once you understand all this, you will understand the secret of "one who places his bed between north and south will have male children" — this is found at midnight, when the body has already quieted from the boiling of the nature of the food eaten, and the constitution of the body is clear.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:78: And what is said, "between north and south," between cold and heat — it is known that every man born from a cold drop will always be a fool and simpleton, and one born from a hot drop will be an angry, wrathful person; but one born from a drop balanced between heat and cold will always be wise, precious of spirit, a man of understanding, and will be moderate in his opinions among people. Of this it is said (1 Samuel 1:11), "and give to Your maidservant seed of men" — [balanced] men. And what our Sages of blessed memory expounded in the Gemara, Berachot (31b), "neither dark nor fair, [neither wise] nor foolish, neither tall nor short" — for all the [balanced] qualities occur in a person when his constitution is between cold and heat, which is the secret of "between north and south" — and this is the secret of "male children" that we have mentioned.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:79: But what they said, "his wife will not miscarry" — there is a genuine principle in this matter, and I shall open for you gates of light in this. You already know what our Sages of blessed memory said (Yoma 82b) regarding that pregnant woman who smelled [food] etc., "they whispered to her and it whispered" — this is [the pattern of] "between north and south"; of her the verse says (Jeremiah 1:5), "before I formed you in the womb" etc. And that pregnant woman to whom "they whispered and it did not whisper" — this inclines toward the southern direction; of her the verse says (Psalms 58:4), "the wicked are estranged from the womb." And it is known that the cause of miscarriage is the womb being roused toward one of the extremes — whether toward hunger or toward craving she miscarries, whether toward heat or toward cold; for when the womb is balanced it will never miscarry, like the scale in a just balance, that the pans not tip toward either side. If so, [the woman] "to whom they whispered and it did not whisper" inclines from the middle extreme, and is close to miscarrying if she is not fed from the thing she smelled. And should you say, but even if she is righteous and smelled [the food], even though she smelled it, she has returned to the middle balance [so why the difference]? [This point requires further reflection.]
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:80: If so, understand and consider the time proper for a person to have relations, and you will merit children fit for [Torah] instruction. We have thus included in this way three timings for conjugal duty: with respect to the days, with respect to food, and with respect to the hours.
